sentences.nl: Vandaag oefenen we Nederlandse zinnen, met de grammatica van #dutchgrammar-2 les 7, over onderschikkende voegwoorden.
sentences.en: Today we are practicing Dutch sentences with the grammar from #dutchgrammar-2 lesson 7, about subordinating conjunctions.

sentences.nl: Na dit type voegwoord komt een bijzin.
sentences.en: After this type of conjunction comes a subordinate clause.
sentences.explanation:
## 1. Literal Translation  
• After this type conjunction comes a subordinate clause.

## 2. Grammar Explanation and Extensions  
• "Na" is a preposition meaning "after," followed by a noun phrase or a clause.  
• "Dit type voegwoord" means "this type of conjunction," where "type" is a noun and "voegwoord" means "conjunction."  
• The verb "komt" is in the third person singular present tense, meaning "comes."  
• "Een bijzin" is a noun phrase meaning "a subordinate clause," where "bijzin" is the noun.

Extra Dutch phrases:  
• "Na het eten ga ik wandelen." (After the meal, I go for a walk.)  
• "Na het werk kijk ik televisie." (After work, I watch television.)  
• "Na de les studeer ik in de bibliotheek." (After the class, I study in the library.)

## 3. Create a New Example  
• "Na dit soort weer moeten we binnen blijven." (After this kind of weather, we must stay indoors.)

## 4. Culture Note (If there is any)
• No related culture notes.

sentences.nl: En een bijzin heeft een andere woordvolgorde.
sentences.en: And a subordinate clause has a different word order.

sentences.nl: Het is daarom heel belangrijk, om deze les van #dutchgrammar goed te leren!
sentences.en: It is therefore very important to learn this lesson from #dutchgrammar well!

sentences.nl: Het is niet zo moeilijk,, maar veel buitenlanders die Nederlands leren,, doen dit verkeerd.
sentences.en: It's not that difficult, but many foreigners who learn Dutch do this wrong.
sentences.explanation:
## 1. Literal Translation  
• It is not so difficult, but many foreigners who Dutch learn, do this wrong.

## 2. Grammar Explanation and Extensions  
• "Het is niet zo moeilijk" uses a straightforward subject-verb structure with "niet zo" (not so) to indicate a degree of difficulty.  
• "Veel buitenlanders die Nederlands leren, doen dit verkeerd" uses a relative clause introduced by "die," meaning "who." The clause "die Nederlands leren" describes "buitenlanders."  
• The main clause "doen dit verkeerd" shows the use of "doen" (to do) as an auxiliary verb to indicate incorrect action.

• Additional Examples:  
  - "Het is niet zo ver." (It is not so far.)  
  - "Veel mensen die reizen, genieten ervan." (Many people who travel, enjoy it.)  
  - "Ze doen het goed." (They do it well.)

## 3. Create a New Example  
• Het is niet zo ingewikkeld, maar veel studenten die wiskunde studeren, maken fouten. (It is not so complicated, but many students who study mathematics make mistakes.)

## 4. Culture Note (If there is any)  
• Learning Dutch can be challenging for foreigners, especially due to the pronunciation and word order, which are different from English. Many learners struggle with these aspects, which is a common topic of discussion among Dutch language learners.

sentences.nl: Dan ga ik met mijn man samenwonen.
sentences.en: Then I will move in with my husband.
sentences.explanation:
## 1. Literal Translation  
• Then go I with my husband cohabit.

## 2. Grammar Explanation and Extensions  
• The sentence structure follows a typical Dutch order: Time - Verb - Subject - Rest of the sentence. "Dan" (Then) is a time adverb influencing the verb position.  
• "Samenwonen" is a separable verb, where "samen" (together) is a prefix that can be detached.  
• "Met mijn man" indicates accompaniment and uses the preposition "met" (with).

Extra phrases:  
– Morgen ga ik met mijn vriend wandelen. (Tomorrow I go with my friend for a walk.)  
– Daarna zal ik met haar praten. (Afterwards I will talk with her.)  
– We gaan samen een huis kopen. (We are going to buy a house together.)

## 3. Create a New Example  
• Volgende maand ga ik met mijn zus op reis. (Next month I will go on a trip with my sister.)

## 4. Culture Note (If there is any)  
• In the Netherlands, cohabitation without marriage is quite common and socially accepted. Many couples choose to live together before considering marriage.

sentences.nl: Ik doe deze cursus,, omdat ik na de zomer, bij het Nederlandse consulaat in Dubai, een examen moet doen.
sentences.en: I am taking this course because I have to take an exam at the Dutch consulate in Dubai after the summer.
sentences.explanation:
## 1. Literal Translation  
• I do this course, because I after the summer, at the Dutch consulate in Dubai, an exam must do.

## 2. Grammar Explanation and Extensions  
• **Subordinate Clause:** "omdat ik na de zomer, bij het Nederlandse consulaat in Dubai, een examen moet doen" is a subordinate clause introduced by "omdat" (because), which pushes the verb to the end.  
• **Word Order:** In Dutch, time ("na de zomer") usually comes before place ("bij het Nederlandse consulaat"), just like in this sentence.  
• **Modal Verb:** "moet" (must) is a modal verb, which affects the main verb "doen" (do).  
• **Examples:**  
  - "Omdat ik morgen vroeg opsta, ga ik nu slapen." (Because I get up early tomorrow, I am going to sleep now.)  
  - "Ik doe dit, omdat het moet." (I do this because it must be done.)  
  - "Na de lunch ga ik wandelen." (After lunch, I am going for a walk.)

## 3. Create a New Example  
• "Ik neem deze baan, omdat ik dichter bij huis wil werken." (I am taking this job because I want to work closer to home.)

## 4. Culture Note (If there is any)  
• In the Netherlands, taking language or integration exams might be necessary for non-native speakers who wish to work or live there long-term.

sentences.nl: Welk examen? — Het ‘basisexamen inburgering buitenland’.
sentences.en: Which exam? — The 'basic civic integration examination abroad'.
sentences.explanation:
## 1. Literal Translation  
• Which exam? — The 'basic integration exam abroad'.

## 2. Grammar Explanation and Extensions  
• "Welk" is an interrogative pronoun used to ask "which" or "what" about something specific.  
• "Het" is the definite article "the" used for neuter nouns.  
• "Basisexamen" is a compound noun formed by "basis" (basic) and "examen" (exam). In Dutch, compound nouns are written as one word.  
• "Inburgering" refers to integration, specifically for newcomers to Dutch society.  
• "Buitenland" means "abroad" and is used here as a noun.  
• Example: "Welke kleur?" (Which color?)  
• Example: "Het examen was moeilijk." (The exam was difficult.)

## 3. Create a New Example  
• "Welke film? — De nieuwe 'Avengers' film." (Which movie? — The new 'Avengers' movie.)

## 4. Culture Note (If there is any)  
• The "basisexamen inburgering buitenland" is a real exam for immigrants who want to live in the Netherlands. It's part of the integration process to assess basic Dutch language knowledge and understanding of Dutch society.

sentences.nl: Oh, het inburgeringsexamen…
sentences.en: Oh, the integration exam…
sentences.explanation:
## 1. Literal Translation  
• Oh, the integration exam...

## 2. Grammar Explanation and Extensions  
• "Het" is a definite article for neuter nouns. "Inburgeringsexamen" is a compound noun made of "inburgering" (integration) and "examen" (exam).  
• The use of "Oh" here is an interjection expressing a reaction or realization.  
• Compound nouns are common in Dutch and can often be lengthy.

  - De auto-ongelukken zijn toegenomen. (The car accidents have increased.)
  - Mijn huiswerk is nog niet af. (My homework is not finished yet.)
  - Het weerbericht voorspelt regen. (The weather forecast predicts rain.)

## 3. Create a New Example  
• Oh, de regen vandaag... (Oh, the rain today...)

## 4. Culture Note (If there is any)  
• The "inburgeringsexamen" is a test that some immigrants to the Netherlands must pass to gain permanent residency or citizenship. It covers Dutch language and culture.

sentences.nl: Nee Pablo… Het ‘basisexamen inburgering buitenland’, is niet hetzelfde als het inburgeringsexamen.
sentences.en: No Pablo… The 'basic integration exam abroad' is not the same as the integration exam.

sentences.nl: Het ‘basisexamen inburgering buitenland’, is een examen op A1 niveau, bij het consulaat of de ambassade.
sentences.en: The 'civic integration examination abroad' is an A1 level exam at the consulate or embassy.
sentences.explanation:
## 1. Literal Translation  
• The 'basic exam integration abroad', is an exam at A1 level, at the consulate or the embassy.

## 2. Grammar Explanation and Extensions  
• **Noun Phrase with Quotation Marks**: "Het ‘basisexamen inburgering buitenland’" uses quotation marks to specify the name of an exam. This is common for official titles or specific terms.  
• **Word Order**: The sentence follows a straightforward structure: Subject + Verb + Object.  
• **Prepositions**: "bij het consulaat of de ambassade" means "at the consulate or the embassy." The preposition "bij" is used for locations.  

Extra phrases:  
• "Het ‘rijexamen’, is een test voor je rijbewijs." (The 'driving test', is a test for your driver's license.)  
• "Hij werkt bij de universiteit." (He works at the university.)  
• "Het examen is op B2 niveau." (The exam is at B2 level.)

## 3. Create a New Example  
• "Het ‘taalvaardigheidsexamen’, is een test op B2 niveau, bij de universiteit." (The 'language proficiency exam', is a test at B2 level, at the university.)

## 4. Culture Note (If there is any)  
The "basisexamen inburgering buitenland" is part of the Dutch immigration process. It is often required for individuals who want to settle in the Netherlands from outside the EU. The exam tests basic Dutch language skills and knowledge of Dutch society.

sentences.nl: Je moet voor het examen slagen, om een ‘MVV’ te krijgen.
sentences.en: You must pass the exam to get an 'MVV'.
sentences.explanation:
## 1. Literal Translation  
• You must for the exam pass, in order to a 'MVV' to get.

## 2. Grammar Explanation and Extensions  
• "Je moet" is a modal verb phrase meaning "you must" or "you have to," indicating obligation.  
• "Voor het examen slagen" uses the preposition "voor" to indicate the object of the verb "slagen" (to pass).  
• "Om ... te krijgen" is an infinitive construction indicating purpose, translated as "in order to get."

Examples:  
• Je moet voor de toets leren. (You have to study for the test.)  
• Hij slaagde voor zijn rijexamen. (He passed his driving test.)  
• Ze werkt hard om haar doel te bereiken. (She works hard in order to reach her goal.)

## 3. Create a New Example  
• Je moet vroeg opstaan om de trein te halen. (You have to get up early to catch the train.)

## 4. Culture Note (If there is any)  
• An 'MVV' is a "Machtiging tot Voorlopig Verblijf," a temporary residence permit necessary for some foreigners to enter the Netherlands for a stay longer than 90 days.

sentences.nl: Wat is dat, een ‘MVV’? — Een ‘MVV’ is een machtiging tot voorlopig verblijf.
sentences.en: What is that, an 'MVV'? — An 'MVV' is an authorization for temporary stay.
sentences.explanation:
## 1. Literal Translation  
• What is that, a 'MVV'? — A 'MVV' is an authorization for temporary stay.

## 2. Grammar Explanation and Extensions  
• **Word Order:** The sentence starts with a question word "Wat" (What), followed by "is" (is) and "dat" (that). This is a typical structure for forming questions in Dutch, where the verb precedes the subject.  
• **Nouns and Articles:** "Een" is an indefinite article meaning "a" or "an." Dutch articles can be "de" or "het" for definite articles, but "een" remains constant for indefinite ones.  
• **Acronym Explanation:** "MVV" stands for "machtiging tot voorlopig verblijf," which is a specific document or permit in Dutch immigration law.

Examples:  
– Wat is jouw naam? (What is your name?)  
– Een ‘BSN’ is een burgerservicenummer. (A 'BSN' is a citizen service number.)  
– Wat betekent dat, een ‘OV-chipkaart’? (What does that mean, an 'OV-chipkaart'?)

## 3. Create a New Example  
• Wat is dat, een ‘BSN’? — Een ‘BSN’ is een burgerservicenummer. (What is that, a 'BSN'? — A 'BSN' is a citizen service number.)

## 4. Culture Note (If there is any)  
• The "MVV" is a crucial document for non-EU citizens who wish to stay in the Netherlands for more than three months. It is part of the Dutch immigration process and is often one of the first steps in applying for a residence permit.

sentences.nl: Wat een moeilijk woord!

sentences.nl: Dat is een visum, om langer dan 90 dagen in Nederland te blijven.
sentences.en: That is a visa, to stay in the Netherlands for longer than 90 days.
sentences.explanation:
## 1. Literal Translation  
• That is a visa, to longer than 90 days in the Netherlands to stay.

## 2. Grammar Explanation and Extensions  
• The sentence uses a relative pronoun "om" to introduce a purpose clause, similar to "in order to" in English.  
• "Langer dan 90 dagen" is a comparative structure meaning "longer than 90 days."  
• "Te blijven" is an infinitive phrase. The infinitive "blijven" means "to stay," and "te" is a particle used before infinitives to express purpose or intention.

Extra examples:  
• "Hij heeft een vergunning, om hier te werken." (He has a permit to work here.)  
• "Ze kocht een boek, om meer te leren." (She bought a book to learn more.)  
• "We hebben een kaartje nodig, om de trein te nemen." (We need a ticket to take the train.)

## 3. Create a New Example  
• "Dat is een kaartje, om naar het concert te gaan." (That is a ticket to go to the concert.)

## 4. Culture Note (If there is any)  
• In the Netherlands, staying longer than 90 days typically requires a special visa or residence permit. This is important for non-EU citizens who plan to live, work, or study in the country for an extended period.

sentences.nl: Is dat een visum voor altijd? — Nee dat is geen visum voor altijd,, omdat het een voorlopige vergunning is.
sentences.en: Is that a visa forever? — No, that is not a visa forever, because it is a temporary permit.
sentences.explanation:
## 1. Literal Translation  
• Is that a visa for always? — No that is not a visa for always, because it a temporary permit is.

## 2. Grammar Explanation and Extensions  
• The sentence uses a question structure with "is dat" (is that), which is a common way to form yes/no questions in Dutch.  
• "Voor altijd" means "forever" or "for always," a fixed phrase to indicate permanence.  
• "Omdat" introduces a subordinate clause, causing the verb "is" to be placed at the end of the clause, which is a typical word order pattern in Dutch subordinate clauses.  
• Example 1: "Is dat jouw boek?" (Is that your book?)  
• Example 2: "Nee, dat is geen probleem, omdat ik al klaar ben." (No, that is not a problem, because I am already done.)

## 3. Create a New Example  
• "Is dit jouw hond?" — "Nee, dat is mijn buurmans hond, omdat ik geen huisdieren heb." (Is this your dog? — No, that is my neighbor's dog, because I don't have pets.)

## 4. Culture Note (If there is any)  
• The concept of "voor altijd" might reflect the Dutch preference for clarity and directness, especially in legal or bureaucratic contexts like visas and permits, where terms need to be clearly defined.

sentences.nl: Met dit visum kun je naar Nederland komen,, maar in Nederland, moet je het inburgeringsexamen doen.
sentences.en: With this visa, you can come to the Netherlands, but in the Netherlands, you must take the integration exam.

sentences.nl: En dan pas krijg je een verblijfsvergunning.
sentences.en: And only then will you get a residence permit.
sentences.explanation:
## 1. Literal Translation  
• And then only get you a residence permit.

## 2. Grammar Explanation and Extensions  
• The sentence uses "en dan pas," which implies a sequence where something will only happen after certain conditions are met. "Pas" adds emphasis on the timing or order.  
• "Krijg je" is an example of inversion in Dutch, where the subject "je" comes after the verb "krijg" in main clauses when the sentence does not start with the subject.  
• The word "verblijfsvergunning" is a compound noun, combining "verblijf" (residence) and "vergunning" (permit).  
• Extra Examples:  
  - "Eerst moet je examen doen, en dan pas kun je naar de universiteit." (First, you must take exams, and only then can you go to university.)  
  - "Je moet het formulier invullen, en dan pas mag je binnenkomen." (You must fill in the form, and only then may you enter.)  
  - "Ze hebben hard gewerkt, en dan pas hebben ze vakantie." (They worked hard, and only then do they have a vacation.)

## 3. Create a New Example  
• Eerst moet je goedkeuring krijgen, en dan pas kun je beginnen. (First, you need to get approval, and only then can you start.)

## 4. Culture Note (If there is any)  
• In the Netherlands, obtaining a residence permit can be a lengthy process that involves meeting specific criteria. The use of "en dan pas" highlights the often sequential nature of bureaucratic procedures.

sentences.nl: Nou, dat klinkt erg moeilijk.
sentences.en: Well, that sounds very difficult.

sentences.nl: Gelukkig geldt dat niet voor mij.
sentences.en: Fortunately, that does not apply to me.
sentences.explanation:
## 1. Literal Translation  
• Luckily applies that not for me.

## 2. Grammar Explanation and Extensions  
• "Gelukkig" is an adverb meaning "luckily" or "fortunately."  
• "Geldt" is the third person singular form of the verb "gelden," meaning "to apply" or "to be valid."  
• "Dat" is a conjunction here meaning "that."  
• "Niet" is used for negation, positioned before the phrase it negates.  
• "Voor" is a preposition meaning "for."  
• "Mij" is the object pronoun "me."

• Example: "Dat geldt voor iedereen." (That applies to everyone.)  
• Example: "Voor hem geldt een andere regel." (A different rule applies to him.)  
• Example: "Gelukkig regent het niet." (Luckily, it’s not raining.)

## 3. Create a New Example  
• "Gelukkig ben ik niet ziek." (Luckily, I am not sick.)

## 4. Culture Note (If there is any)  
• [No related culture note]

sentences.nl: Waarom geldt dat niet voor jou? — Dat geldt niet voor mij, omdat ik uit Polen kom.
sentences.en: Why does that not apply to you? — It does not apply to me because I am from Poland.

sentences.nl: En EU-burgers kunnen in elk ander EU-land wonen en werken.
sentences.en: And EU citizens can live and work in any other EU country.
sentences.explanation:
## 1. Literal Translation  
• And EU-citizens can in every other EU-country live and work.

## 2. Grammar Explanation and Extensions  
• "En" is a coordinating conjunction meaning "and."  
• "EU-burgers" refers to citizens of the European Union.  
• "Kunnen" is the plural form of "can," indicating ability or permission.  
• "In elk ander EU-land" means "in every other EU-country," demonstrating prepositional use for location.  
• "Wonen en werken" are infinitive verbs meaning "to live and work."

• Extra Sentences:  
  - "Hij kan in Nederland wonen." (He can live in the Netherlands.)  
  - "Zij willen in een ander land werken." (They want to work in another country.)  
  - "Wij mogen in dat huis wonen." (We are allowed to live in that house.)

## 3. Create a New Example  
• Nederlanders mogen in elk EU-land reizen. (Dutch people are allowed to travel in every EU-country.)

## 4. Culture Note (If there is any)  
• The sentence highlights the EU policy of free movement, allowing EU citizens the right to live and work in any member state. This is a fundamental aspect of EU citizenship aimed at fostering integration and cooperation among member states.

sentences.nl: Wat is de IND? — Dat is de immigratie- en naturalisatie dienst.
sentences.en: What is the IND? — That is the Immigration and Naturalisation Service.
sentences.explanation:
## 1. Literal Translation  
• What is the IND? — That is the immigration and naturalization service.

## 2. Grammar Explanation and Extensions  
• "Wat is de IND?" uses the structure for asking questions in Dutch, where the verb ("is") precedes the subject ("de IND").  
• "Dat is de immigratie- en naturalisatie dienst" follows a simple declarative structure with "Dat is" meaning "That is." The compound noun "immigratie- en naturalisatie dienst" describes an official government agency.  
• Extra phrases:  
  - "Wat is jouw naam?" (What is your name?)  
  - "Dat is mijn fiets." (That is my bike.)  
  - "Wie is de leraar?" (Who is the teacher?)

## 3. Create a New Example  
• "Wat is het KNMI? — Dat is het Koninklijk Nederlands Meteorologisch Instituut." (What is the KNMI? — That is the Royal Netherlands Meteorological Institute.)

## 4. Culture Note (If there is any)  
• The IND, or "Immigratie- en Naturalisatiedienst," is a key governmental body in the Netherlands responsible for handling immigration and naturalization processes. It plays a crucial role for those seeking residency or citizenship in the Netherlands.

sentences.nl: Op hun website staat veel informatie.

sentences.nl: Zij behandelen alle aanvragen, om in Nederland te wonen, of Nederlander te worden.
sentences.en: They handle all applications to live in the Netherlands or to become a Dutch citizen.
sentences.explanation:
## 1. Literal Translation  
• They handle all applications, to in the Netherlands to live, or Dutch to become.

## 2. Grammar Explanation and Extensions  
• The sentence uses "om...te" to indicate purpose or intention, which is equivalent to "to" or "in order to" in English.  
• "Te wonen" and "te worden" are infinitive verb forms preceded by "te," similar to the English "to live" and "to become."  
• The word order in Dutch places the main verb at the end of the clause, common in subordinate clauses.

  Examples:  
  • Zij proberen om de beste oplossing te vinden. (They try to find the best solution.)  
  • Hij werkt hard om zijn doelen te bereiken. (He works hard to achieve his goals.)  
  • We besloten om vroeg te vertrekken. (We decided to leave early.)

## 3. Create a New Example  
• Zij willen om in Amsterdam te studeren, of ervaring op te doen. (They want to study in Amsterdam, or to gain experience.)

## 4. Culture Note (If there is any)  
• In the Netherlands, there are specific legal processes and criteria for applications to live in the country or to obtain Dutch citizenship. The process can be complex and often requires handling by official institutions like the IND (Immigratie- en Naturalisatiedienst).

sentences.nl: Voor mensen buiten de EU zonder Nederlandse baan, is het niet zo makkelijk…
sentences.en: For people outside the EU without a Dutch job, it is not so easy…
sentences.explanation:
## 1. Literal Translation  
• For people outside the EU without Dutch job, is it not so easy…

## 2. Grammar Explanation and Extensions  
• **Preposition use:** "Voor" means "for," indicating the group of people affected.  
• **Word order:** The sentence begins with a prepositional phrase "Voor mensen buiten de EU," so the main clause "is het niet zo makkelijk" follows with the subject "het" after the verb "is" due to the inversion rule in Dutch.  
• **Negation:** "Niet zo makkelijk" means "not so easy," where "niet" negates the adjective "makkelijk."  
• **Example phrases:**
  - "Voor kinderen onder de vijf jaar is de toegang gratis." (For children under five years old, the entry is free.)
  - "Voor mensen zonder auto, zijn er genoeg openbaar vervoer opties." (For people without a car, there are plenty of public transport options.)
  - "Buiten de stad is het rustiger." (Outside the city, it is quieter.)

## 3. Create a New Example  
• Voor studenten zonder boeken, is het moeilijker om te studeren. (For students without books, it is more difficult to study.)

## 4. Culture Note (If there is any)  
• The phrase refers to the complexities faced by non-EU residents trying to find work in the Netherlands, highlighting the country’s strict immigration and work regulations.
